text:
Diego: Quick question for folks 1414 Do we ship starter sample projects as a modal popover on first-run or an inline shelf at the top of the console? I9m leaning shelf (less interruptive).
Ava: Shelf please. Modals break keyboard flow and feel like a gate. Shelf can be subtle and persistent.
Sam: +1. In our usability tests users dismissed modals. A compact shelf with 2 starters increased clickthrough.
Ravi: Shelf impacts header spacing. Dev estimate: ~1 day markup/CSS + 1 day animation polish. Popover is faster but needs extra a11y fixes.
Lina: Accessibility notes if we do shelf: must be focusable, provide a skip-link, announce only on first render via aria-live, and ensure contrast on card labels meets AA. Keyboard expand/collapse must not trap focus.
Diego: Thoughts on hybrid? Shelf for first-run, then collapsed for returning users.
Ava: Hybrid is neat. For first-run show "Explore starter projects" CTA and announce via aria-live. For returners show collapsed rail with chevron.
Sam: Also should tie samples to the quickstart checklist so completing a sample marks a step done. That helps activation.
Ravi: Technical approach: use a route param to keep it stateless e.g. /projects/:id?onboard_sample=vector-chat. Simple and easy to link.
Ravi: Code snippet:
```
<Link to={`/projects/${p.id}?onboard_sample=${sample.slug}`}>Open sample</Link>
```
Ava: Copy option for shelf header: "Try a starter project 14 3 quick demos" vs "Sample projects". Which performs better?
Sam: "Try a starter project" is more action-oriented. Add microcopy: "Complete one to see Redwood in your product"
Diego: Agreed. Also we need analytics: shelf_shown, shelf_collapsed, shelf_sample_started. Sam, can you add a small funnel?
Sam: Yep. Will add events and a pulse retention test for week 1.
Lina: A11y checklist for the PR: 1) keyboard order verified, 2) aria-live only first-render, 3) high-contrast labels, 4) focus return when any sample modal closes. I'll add this to review checklist.
Ava: Deliverables for design handoff: A) compact chip rail, B) thumbnail shelf, C) collapsed summary. We should A/B compact vs thumbnail for new signups.
Diego: Timeline: want MVP next sprint. Ravi, is 2-3 dev days realistic?
Ravi: Estimate 3 dev days + 1 QA day + a11y pass. If we skip animations maybe 2 dev days.
Diego: MVP scope: compact chip rail, route param linking, analytics. Thumbnail-rich shelf as follow-up.
onboard-bot: Reminder: design handoff doc requested 14 attach Figma link and component tokens by EOD Fri.
Ava: Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/starter-shelf 14 contains tokens and states.
Diego: Final decision: implement compact shelf initially, auto-collapse for returning users, use route param for sample launch, instrument analytics, follow-up A/B with thumbnails. Lina to add a11y checklist to PR. Sam to add analytics funnel. Ravi to open spike branch.
Lina: Will watch PR and run keyboard/a11y tests. :thumbsup:
Sam: Drafting event list and pulse test plan tomorrow.
Ravi: Starting branch now, will ping on PR.
Diego: Thanks all. Moving to roadmap board and marking "in sprint" for next cycle. :rocket:
